name: Law of Closure
axiom: The eye completes a broken outline and sees the whole shape it implies.
trigger: A carousel stops exactly at the screen edge, so nothing signals more content.

checklist.text: Let the next card peek past the edge instead of ending the list flush with the viewport.
Draw icons as open strokes where the missing segment does not change the meaning.
Use skeleton shapes that outline the incoming content rather than a centred spinner.
Ask users whether a scrollable list has more items; a no is a closure failure.

antiPattern.violation: A carousel snaps flush to the margins, so the row reads as complete and nobody swipes.
antiPattern.remediation: One card sits two-thirds off the edge, so the row visibly continues.
